scope: Targeted checkpoint-started logical play. Baseline authored actions excluded; not full campaign or human fun proof.

sessions.report: I stopped voluntarily in episode 9 without reaching the crew portrait. This was fresh play only after an authored later checkpoint, not a full-campaign run or a claim about human players. The table and personal pictures were an appealing modest goal; I wanted to see the crew settled together. Padding the rope into a sling and securing the sled made sense after my initial padding-on-sled attempt failed. After that I could not find the intended recovery action. Placing the secured sled on the cargo shoulder only said Placed, with no progress. The secured-sled hint gave no combinations or settings. I carried it to Recovery camp, where its hint still gave none; I then looked for hauling equipment on the Survey recovery route. Crawler plus sled failed. I brought the rover and tow eye back, made and fitted a tow line, but rover plus secured sled also failed, and the rover hint gave no combinations or settings. Carrying the supposedly abandoned cargo freely between places while not recovering it was confusing. The trips and repeated empty hints became uninteresting; I stopped because I was hunting an unstated rule rather than acting on the appealing story. I would have continued if a concrete recovery affordance or explanatory response had kept that story moving. I do not know whether the blockage is the checkpoint, my misunderstanding, or the game rule, and I did not inspect hidden files.

Targeted later-chapter trial from an authored checkpoint, not full-campaign play. I completed electricity stage 17 and communications stage 18, then stopped voluntarily at the chapter boundary. The initial compass/current, magnet/coil and ring/log pairings were obvious in a pleasant way. Preserving quiet readings and distinguishing change from mere magnetic presence made me want the generator payoff; the final mechanical-energy explanation felt earned. I stalled after making the change argument because I had overlooked compass plus bar magnet. Hints on the argument, wire comparison and generator all had no partners, which briefly felt like a dead end; a compass hint restored momentum, and the direction-map branch then made sense. Communications was less engaging mechanically: I tried adding redundancy to the encoded message before sending it, and tried applying correction to the corrupted transmission, but both were rejected. The accepted order felt like arranging teaching labels rather than actually protecting and repairing a message. The explicit prefix-code example and 1.5-versus-2-bit calculation were the strongest reward there. Familiar direct combinations were often satisfying, but repeated abstract combinations and repeated cautions started to feel routine. I am stopping because these two resolved exhibits are a satisfying session and the next replication title does not make me eager to start another chain, not because I am blocked or required to stop. Four hints, seven rejected drops, no undo or revisits in my fresh play. This is my logical-interface experience, not a claim about human players or visual/touch usability.

Voluntary stop after completing Food for the crossing (stage 21), before Water for everyone. This was fresh logical-interface play from an authored stage-18 checkpoint, not a full-campaign or human-player claim. I continued because I wanted to discover the pond life, then enjoyed making a flora and provisions for the gathering. Sand plus glass making a lens, collecting pond water with the bowl, observing a leaf through the lens, cider changing to vinegar, and netting fish from the shore were satisfying. Botany was my favourite complete sequence: observe, draw, then join the drawing with the preserved specimen collection. The food chapter was straightforward and pleasantly so, not a difficulty problem. Weather was more routine, and I expected windsock plus paper to make a wind record by analogy with rain-gauge plus paper; it did not. I used two hints in optics, for glass and lens. Glass plus planks making a glass slide remained obscure to me. I also tried plant plus bound-book before learning the plant first needed paper, which felt a fussy distinction. My biggest disappointment was making both Microscope and Pond slide, then getting No new combination here when I put the slide on the microscope. The invitation promised a country in a drop, but I never got an observation payoff there. Making the objects completed the request instead. By the end I wanted the actual gathering, not another preparation list; the next Water for everyone invitation did not pull me onward now. No tool or permission blocker. No visits, undo, or hidden-file inspection; earlier earned equipment and history were supplied by the checkpoint.
